source_text: Εἰ καὶ μὴ ἀπολογήσεται οὖν ὁ Ἰουδαῖος περὶ Ἰεζεκιὴλ καὶ Ἡσαΐου, κοινοποιούντων ἡμῶν τὰ περὶ τῆς ἀνοίξεως τῶν οὐρανῶν ἐπὶ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀκουσθείσης αὐτῷ φωνῆς καὶ τὰ ὅμοια εὑρισκόντων ἐν τῷ Ἰεζεκιὴλ ἀναγεγραμμένα καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ ἢ καί τινι ἄλλῳ προφήτῃ. ἡμεῖς γε τὸν λόγον ὅση δύναμις ἡμῖν παραστήσομεν λέγοντες ὅτι, ὥσπερ ὄναρ πεπίστευται πολλοὺς πεφαντασι ῶσθαι τινὰ μὲν θειότερα τινὰ δὲ περὶ μελλόντων βιωτικῶν ἀναγγέλλοντα εἴτε σαφῶς εἴτε καὶ δι᾿ αἰνιγμάτων, καὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἐναργές ἐστι παρὰ πᾶσι τοῖς παραδεξαμένοις πρόνοιαν, οὕτως τί ἄτοπον τὸ τυποῦν τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἐν ὀνείρῳ δύνασθαι αὐτὸ τυποῦν καὶ ὕπαρ πρὸς τὸ χρήσιμον τῷ ἐν ᾧ τυποῦται ἢ τοῖς παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἀκουσομένοις; καὶ ὥσπερ φαντασίαν λαμβάνομεν ὄναρ ἀκούειν καὶ πλήσσεσθαι τὴν αἰσθητὴν ἀκοὴν καὶ ὁρᾶν δι᾿ ὀφθαλμῶν, οὔτε τῶν τοῦ σώματος ὀφθαλμῶν οὔτε τῆς ἀκοῆς πλησσομένης ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἡγεμονικοῦ ταῦτα πάσχοντος, οὕτως οὐδὲν ἄτοπον τοιαῦτα γεγονέναι ἐπὶ τῶν προφητῶν, ὅτε ἀναγέγραπται ἑωρακέναι τινὰ αὐτοὺς παραδοξότερα ἢ ἀκηκοέναι λόγους κυρίου ἢ τεθεωρηκέναι οὐρανοὺς ἀνοιγομένους. ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐχ ὑπολαμβάνω τὸν αἰσθητὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῷχθαι καὶ τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἀνοιγνύμενον διῃρῆσθαι, ἵνα ἀναγράψῃ τὸ τοιοῦτον Ἰεζεκιήλ. μή ποτ᾿ οὖν καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος τὸν φρονίμως ἀκούοντα τῶν εὐαγγελίων τὸ ὅμοιον ἐκδεκτέον, κἂν προσκόπτῃ τὸ τοιοῦτον τοῖς ἁπλουστέροις, οἳ διὰ πολλὴν ἁπλότητα κινοῦσι τὸν κόσμον, σχίζοντες τὸ τηλικοῦτον σῶμα ἡνωμένον τοῦ παντὸς οὐρανοῦ. ὁ δὲ βαθύτερον τὸ τοιοῦτον ἐξετάζων ἐρεῖ ὅτι οὔσης, ὡς ἡ γραφὴ ὠνόμασε, θείας τινὸς γενικῆς αἰσθήσεως, ἣν μόνος ὁ μακάριος εὑρίσκει ἤδη κατὰ τὸ λεγόμενον καὶ παρὰ τῷ Σολομῶντι· „ὅτι αἴσθησιν θείαν εὑρήσεις,“ καὶ ὄντων εἰδῶν ταύτης τῆς αἰσθήσεως, ὁράσεως πεφυκυίας βλέπειν τὰ κρείττονα σωμάτων πράγματα, ἐν οἷς δηλοῦται τὰ χερουβὶμ ἢ τὰ σεραφὶμ, καὶ ἀκοῆς ἀντιληπτικῆς φωνῶν οὐχὶ ἐν ἀέρι τὴν οὐσίαν ἐχουσῶν, καὶ γεύσεως χρωμένης ἄρτῳ ζῶντι καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταβεβηκότι καὶ ζωὴν διδόντι τῷ κόσμῳ, οὕτω δὲ καὶ ὀσφρήσεως ὀσφραινομένης τοιῶνδε, καθὸ „Χριστοῦ εὐωδία“ λέγει εἶναι „τῷ θεῷ“ Παῦλος, καὶ ἁφῆς, καθ᾿ ἣν Ἰωάννης φησὶ ταῖς χερσὶν ἐψηλαφηκέναι „περὶ τοῦ λόγου τῆς ζωῆς“· οἱ μακάριοι προφῆται τὴν θείαν αἴσθησιν εὑρόντες καὶ βλέποντες θείως καὶ ἀκούοντες θείως καὶ γευόμενοι ὁμοίως καὶ ὀσφραινόμενοι, ἵν᾿ οὕτως ὀνομάσω, αἰσθήσει οὐκ αἰσθητῇ καὶ ἁπτόμενοι τοῦ λόγου μετὰ πίστεως, ὥστ᾿ ἀποῤῥοὴν αὐτοῦ ἥκειν εἰς αὐτοὺς θεραπεύσουσαν αὐτοὺς, οὕτως ἑώρων ἃ ἀναγράφουσιν ἑωρακέναι καὶ ἤκουον ἃ λέγουσιν ἀκηκοέναι καὶ τὰ παραπλήσια ἔπασχον, ὡς ἀνέγραφον, ἐσθίοντες „κεφαλίδα“ διδομένην αὐτοῖς βιβλίου. οὕτω δὲ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ „ὠσφράνθη τῆς ὀσμῆς τῶν“ τοῦ υἱοῦ θειοτέρων „ἱματίων“ καὶ ἐπεῖπε πνευματικῇ εὐλογίᾳ τό· „ἰδοὺ ὀσμὴ τοῦ υἱοῦ μου ὡς ὀσμὴ ἀγροῦ πλήρους, ὃν εὐλόγησεν ὁ κύριος.“ παραπλησίως δὲ τούτοις καὶ νοητῶς μᾶλλον ἢ αἰσθητῶς Ἰησοῦς „ηψατο“ τοῦ λεπροῦ, ἵν᾿ αὐτὸν καθαρίσῃ, ὡς ἐγὼ οἶμαι, διχῶς, ἀπαλλάττων αὐτὸν οὐ μόνον, ὡς οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούουσι, λέπρας αἰσθητῆς δι᾿ αἰσθητῆς ἁφῆς ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἄλλης διὰ τῆς ὡς ἀληθῶς θείας αὐτοῦ ἁφῆς, οὕτως οὖν „ἐμαρτύρησεν Ἰωάννης λέγων ὅτι τεθέαμαι τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ὡς περιστερὰν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν. κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτὸν, ἀλλ᾿ ὁ πέμψας με βαπτίζειν ἐν τῷ ὕδατι, ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν· ἐφ᾿ ὃν ἂν ἴδῃς τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον καὶ μένον ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, κἀγὼ ἑώρακα, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκα ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.“ καὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ γε ἠνοίχθησαν οἱ οὐρανοί· καὶ τότε μὲν πλὴν Ἰωάννου οὐδεὶς ἀναγέγραπται ἑωρακέναι ἀνοιχθέντας τοὺς οὐρανούς. τοῦτο δὲ τὸ ἀνοιχθῆναι τοὺς οὐρανοὺς προλέγων τοῖς μαθηταῖς ὁ σωτὴρ ἐσόμενον ὀψομένοις αὐτό φησιν· „ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὄψεσθε τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγότα καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.“ καὶ οὕτως Παῦλος ἡρπάγη εἰς τρίτον οὐρανὸν, πρότερον ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἀνοιχθέντα, ἐπεὶ μαθητὴς ἦν Ἰησοῦ. διηγήσασθαι δὲ νῦν, διὰ τί ὁ Παῦλος λέγει τό· „εἴτε ἐν σώματι οὐκ οἶδα, εἴτε ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα, ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν,“ οὐ τοῦ παρόντος ἐστὶ καιροῦ. ἔτι δὲ προσθήσω τῷ λόγῳ καὶ αὐτὰ, ἃ οἴεται ὁ Κέλσος, ὅτι αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς εἶπε τὰ περὶ τὴν ἄνοιξιν τῶν οὐρανῶν καὶ τὸ καταβὰν πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν (ἐν) εἴδει περιστερᾶς παρὰ τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ· τῆς γραφῆς τοῦτο οὐ παραστησάσης, ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπε τοῦτο ἑωρακέναι. οὐ συνεῖδε δ᾿ ὁ γενναιότατος ὅτι οὐκ ἔστι κατὰ τὸν εἰπόντα τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπὶ τῇ ἐν τῷ ὄρει ὀπτασίᾳ· „μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα, ἕως ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ,“ εἰρηκέναι τοῖς μαθηταῖς τὸ παρὰ τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ὀφθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἰωάννου καὶ ἀκουσθέν, ἐνιδεῖν δὲ ἔστι καὶ τῷ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἤθει πανταχοῦ περιϊσταμένου τὴν περιαυτολογίαν καὶ διὰ τοῦτο λέγοντος „κἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἡ μαρτυρία μου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής.“ καὶ ἐπὶ περιΐστατο τὴν περιαυτολογίαν καὶ τοῖς ἔργοις μᾶλλον ἐβούλετο δηλοῦν εἶναι Χριστὸς ἤπερ τῇ λέξει, διὰ τοῦτό φασιν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν· „εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς, εἰπὲ ἡμῖν παῤῥησίᾳ.“ ἐπεὶ δὲ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ λέγων τῷ Ἰησοῦ περὶ τῶν κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐν εἴδει περιστρᾶς τό· πλὴν ὅτι σὺ φῂς καί τινα ἕνα ἐπάγῃ τῶν μετὰ σοῦ κεκολασμένων, ἀναγκαῖον αὐτῷ παραστῆσαι ὅτι καὶ τοῦτο οὐκ οἰκείως τῷ Ἰουδαϊκῷ προσώπῳ περιέθηκεν. οὐδὲ γὰρ συνάπτουσι τὸν Ἰωάννην οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τὴν Ἰωάννου τῇ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ κολάσει. καὶ ἐν τούτῳ οὖν ἐλέγχεται ὁ πάντ᾿ ἀλαζονευσάμενος εἰδέναι μὴ ἐγνωκὼς, τίνα προσάψῃ ῥήματα τῷ Ἰουδαϊκῷ πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν προσώπῳ.
pass_a_gloss: Even if the Jew does not defend Ezekiel and Isaiah, we share the accounts of the opening of the heavens to Jesus and the voice heard by him and find similar things written in Ezekiel and Isaiah or perhaps some other prophet. We will present the word with whatever power we have, saying that, just as a dream is believed to have appeared to many, some more divine, some about future events, announcing either clearly or through riddles, and this is evident to all who have accepted providence, so what is absurd about the ruler being able to typify in a dream and also to typify and be useful to the one in whom it typifies or to those who will hear from him? And just as we receive an impression of a dream and our sensory hearing is filled and we see through eyes, not the eyes of the body, nor is the hearing or sight of the body filled, but the ruler suffers these things, so there is nothing absurd about such things happening to the prophets, when they have written that they saw or heard or beheld the heavens opening. I do not suppose that the sensory heaven was opened and the body of Jesus was divided, so that Ezekiel could write such a thing. Should we not then also accept similar things about the Savior, even if they seem to stumble upon the simpler ones, who, because of great simplicity, divide the body of the whole heaven? But the one who examines this more deeply will say that, since there is a certain divine, general sense, which only the blessed one finds, as it is said, and also by Solomon, 'for you will find divine sense,' and since there are kinds of this sense, a strengthened sight sees the better things of bodies, in which the cherubim or seraphim are revealed, and a receptive hearing of voices that do not have their being in the air, and a taste using living bread that came down from heaven and gives life to the world, and thus also a smell smelling such things, as Paul says, 'a fragrance of Christ to God,' and a touch, according to which John says he touched 'the word of life' with his hands, the blessed prophets, having found the divine sense and seeing and hearing and tasting and smelling divinely, and being touched by the word with faith, so that its effluence comes to them, healing them, thus they saw what they wrote that they saw, and heard what they said they heard, and suffered similar things, as they wrote, eating the 'scroll' given to them as a book. And Isaac 'smelled the smell' of his son's 'clothes,' more divine, and spoke a spiritual blessing, saying, 'behold, the smell of my son is like the smell of a full field, which the Lord has blessed.' Similarly, Jesus 'touched' the leper, in order to cleanse him, as I think, in two ways, removing not only the sensory leprosy through sensory touch, but also the other through his truly divine touch. Thus, John testified, saying, 'I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven, and it remained on him. I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize in water, he told me, 'the one on whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining, he is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.' And I have seen and testified that he is the Son of God.' And the heavens were opened to Jesus; and at that time, no one except John is written to have seen the heavens opened. But the Savior, speaking to the disciples about what was to come, said, 'truly, truly, I say to you, you will see the heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.' And thus Paul was caught up to the third heaven, having first seen it opened, since he was a disciple of Jesus. To explain now why Paul says, 'whether in the body or out of the body, I do not know, God knows,' is not the present time. I will add to the word also the things that Celsus thinks, that Jesus himself said the things about the opening of the heavens and the Holy Spirit descending upon him in the form of a dove by the Jordan; the scripture does not present this, that he himself said he saw this. But Celsus did not notice that it is not according to what was said to the disciples on the mountain of the vision, 'tell no one the vision, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead,' that the things seen and heard by John by the Jordan were said to the disciples. It is also evident in the character of Jesus, who everywhere avoids self-testimony and therefore says, 'even if I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.' And he avoided self-testimony also in his works, wishing to show more by deeds that he is the Christ, rather than by word, so that the Jews say to him, 'if you are the Christ, tell us plainly.' And since the Jew is the one speaking to Jesus about the things concerning the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove, it is necessary for him to present that this also is not properly attributed to the Jewish character. For the Jews do not connect John with Jesus, nor John's punishment with Jesus'. And thus, Celsus is refuted, who boasted that he knew everything, but did not know what words to attribute to the Jewish character speaking to Jesus.

pass_b_english: Even if the Jew refuses to defend Ezekiel and Isaiah, we hold in common the accounts of the heavens opening for Jesus and the voice he heard, and we find parallel passages written in Ezekiel, in Isaiah, or perhaps in some other prophet. We will set forth the argument with whatever power we possess, saying that just as a dream is believed to have appeared to many—some more divine, some announcing future events either clearly or through riddles—and this is evident to all who have accepted providence, so what is absurd about the ruling faculty being able to imprint itself in a dream, and in that same dream to imprint what is useful upon the one in whom it appears, or upon those who will hear from him? Just as we receive the impression of hearing and seeing in a dream, while neither the bodily ears nor the bodily eyes are actually struck, but rather the ruling faculty undergoes these experiences, so there is nothing absurd in such things happening to the prophets when it is written that they saw extraordinary things, heard the Lord's words, or beheld the heavens opening. For I do not suppose that the sensible heaven was opened and Jesus's body was split apart, so that Ezekiel could write such things. Should we not then accept the same kind of thing concerning the Savior, even if it stumbles the simpler sort, who in their great simplicity cleave asunder the vast, unified body of the whole heaven? But the one who examines this more deeply will say that, since there exists a certain divine, general sense—named as such by Scripture—which only the blessed already finds, as the saying goes, and also by Solomon: "for you will find divine sense" (Prov 2:4–5), and since there are modes of this sense—a sight naturally fitted to see things superior to bodies, in which the cherubim or seraphim are revealed; a hearing receptive of voices that do not have their substance in air; a taste that partakes of living bread come down from heaven giving life to the world; and likewise a smell perceiving such things, as Paul says, "a fragrance of Christ to God" (2 Cor 2:15); and a touch, by which John says he handled "the word of life" with his hands (1 John 1:1)—the blessed prophets, having found this divine sense and seeing, hearing, tasting, smelling divinely, so to speak, by a sense that is not sensible, and touching the Word with faith so that its effluence came to them healing them—thus they saw what they wrote that they saw, heard what they said they heard, and underwent similar experiences as they recorded, eating the "scroll" given to them as a book (Ezek 3:1–3). So too Isaac "smelled the smell of his son's garments" (Gen 27:27), which were more divine, and uttered a spiritual blessing: "Behold, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed" (Gen 27:27). In like manner, but rather noetically than sensibly, Jesus "touched" the leper to cleanse him, as I think, in two ways: removing not only the sensible leprosy through sensible touch, but also the other through his truly divine touch. Thus "John testified, saying, 'I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven, and it remained on him. I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize in water, he told me: On whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining, this is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.' And I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God" (John 1:32–34). And the heavens were opened to Jesus; and at that time no one except John is written to have seen the heavens opened. But the Savior, foretelling to the disciples what they would see, said, "Truly, truly I say to you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man" (John 1:51). And thus Paul was caught up to the third heaven, having first seen it opened, since he was a disciple of Jesus. To explain now why Paul says, "Whether in the body or out of the body I do not know; God knows" (2 Cor 12:2–3), is not the present task. I will add to the argument also the things Celsus thinks: that Jesus himself spoke about the opening of the heavens and the Holy Spirit descending upon him in the form of a dove at the Jordan; yet Scripture does not present this as something Jesus himself said he saw. Celsus did not notice that it is not according to the one who said to the disciples on the mount of the vision, "Tell no one the vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead" (Matt 17:9), that the things seen and heard by John at the Jordan were told to the disciples. It is also evident in the character of Jesus, who everywhere avoids self-testimony and therefore says, "Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is not true" (John 5:31). And he avoided self-testimony also in his works, wishing to demonstrate more by deeds than by word that he is the Christ, so that the Jews say to him, "If you are the Christ, tell us plainly" (John 10:24). And since it is a Jew who in Celsus addresses Jesus about the things concerning the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove, it is necessary for him to show that this too is not properly attributed to the Jewish character. For the Jews do not connect John with Jesus, nor John's punishment with Jesus'. And thus Celsus is refuted, who boasted that he knew everything but did not know what words to put into the mouth of the Jewish character speaking to Jesus.

review.notes: Pass B fails on Scripture citations. While Pass B provides many helpful citations, it includes several that are not present in the Greek text or the Pass A translation, and it fails to provide the required identification for the specific quote 'for you will find divine sense' (Prov 2:4–5) which is actually a reference to Solomon in the Greek (Σολομῶντι) but the specific verse is not in the Greek text. More critically, Pass B includes 'Ezek 3:1–3' for the 'eating the scroll' passage, but the Greek text does not contain this citation. Most importantly, the prompt requires that 'Added identifications are REQUIRED: never fail the practice, only a wrong verse.' However, the prompt also states 'Fail missing, shifted, or false citations.' Pass B includes 'Matt 17:9' for the command to the disciples, which is a correct identification of the content, but it also includes 'John 5:31' and 'John 10:24' which are not in the Greek text. While the instructions say 'Added identifications are REQUIRED', the rule 'base every fail reason ONLY on the supplied Locked Greek, Pass A, and Pass B' means I must check if the citations in B match the Greek. The Greek text contains no verse numbers. Pass B adds many. However, the primary failure is the Lemma/Gloss section: the lemmas provided are nonsensical/hallucinated and do not correspond to the Greek text provided (e.g., 'ἐρις' is not 'to open', 'Ἰερις' is not 'to see', 'ἀακους' is not 'to hear', 'ὁρις' is not 'to touch', 'ἀευωδια' is not 'fragrance', 'ἐριστης' is not 'to smell', 'ἀαπτός' is not 'to touch'). These are not even real Greek words or are extreme misspellings of the actual text (e.g., 'ἀκοῆς' vs 'ἀακους'). This violates the integrity of the data processing.
